method: Every image hash we hold (kdh1, a 64-bit difference hash, see /data/image-hashes.json) is compared with every other one: Hamming distance of the full-image hash and of the hash of the central 70%. A match needs both distances small (full at most 8 bits, centre at most 10 bits of 64) and the two images must come from two different projects. Hashes with little structure (fewer than 6 distinct bytes, or fewer than 16 or more than 48 bits set: skies, flat colour, gradients) are left out because they match unrelated pictures. A picture that matches images of 4 or more other projects is counted as stock or template art and not listed. The same function runs in the browser on /tools/image-check/, so anyone can hash a picture and compare.

kinds.cross: different developers, pages on different websites
kinds.same_site: different developers, both pages on the same website (often a listing portal)
kinds.same_dev: two projects of the same developer

caution: A match means the two project pages we read show the same or a near-identical picture. It is a fact about the pictures, not about the developers: agents, portals and sister brands often reuse a render or an area photo. Check the picture on both pages before drawing any conclusion.
